summary: This note is a documentation page for the ARRAY_REMOVE_AT function, which returns a copy of an ARRAY with the element at a given zero-based position removed. It covers the syntax, arguments (array and position, where negative positions count from the back), return behavior including NULL handling, and a usage note about out-of-range positions. Three examples show removing the first element, removing the last element with -1, and passing a position greater than the array length, which returns the array unchanged.
one_line: Documents the ARRAY_REMOVE_AT function, which returns an array with the element at a given zero-based position removed.
key_facts: ARRAY_REMOVE_AT takes an array and a position and returns an ARRAY with the element at the specified position removed.
The position argument is zero-based, so position 0 refers to the first element.
A negative position is interpreted as an index from the back of the array, so -1 removes the last element.
If the absolute value of the position exceeds the length of the array, the function returns the array without any elements removed.
If the position argument is NULL, the function returns NULL.
